models.description: A user-defined totals formula created and validated on this device.

SPMT projects a game as expected possessions times points per possession. Possessions use the harmonic mean of both teams' paces, so a slow team drags tempo down more than a simple average would. Each team's offense and defense rates (points per possession) are blended with a league prior using weight g / (g + 8), so teams with few games lean on the prior and teams with more games lean on their own data. The prior is 1.025 points per possession per side (2.05 combined), an assumption and not imported data.

matchTotal is the original SPMT formula, with denominator guards that do not change any value, so its earlier tracking record still applies. homeTotal and awayTotal split the same total with an offense-versus-defense matchup: Home points per possession = the average of Home shrunk offense and Away shrunk defense, with 1.6 points added to Home and removed from Away as a home-court allowance (before clamping, Home plus Away equals matchTotal). handicap is Home minus Away from the same rates plus the 3.2-point home-court constant, which is borrowed from the app's validated example and not tuned. straightWin converts that margin to a Home win probability with the algebraic sigmoid 0.5 + 0.48 * m / sqrt(190 + m squared). Because the rates are shrunk hard, margins stay close to the home-court constant early in the season.

decision is a conservative ranker: 0.60 * (opt.prob - 0.5) + 0.25 * (opt.prob - opt.implied_prob) + 0.15 * opt.z / 3 (capped at plus or minus 1), plus a 0.03 bonus for the three totals markets (match, home, away). It then subtracts 1.5 per unit of odds below 1.30 and 0.4 per unit of odds above 2.30, so the #1, #2 and #3 picks favor likelier outcomes at mid-range prices over longshots. opt.ev is not used directly because prob minus implied probability carries the same sign.

Assumptions and limitations: team rates come from season-to-date totals, so early-season samples of 1 to 3 games are noisy. Games against non-Division I opponents can inflate a team's totals (a blank SRS in the data is a warning sign). No SRS, SOS, injuries or roster changes are used, so missing ratings never cause NO DATA. The home-court constants are wrong for neutral-site games. Overtime is not modeled separately. Margin and win probability are rough extensions of a totals model. No accuracy or profitability is claimed; it has only been tested on a small early-season log with no reliable edge shown.

SIET projects a game as expected possessions times points per possession, like SPMT, but it matches each side's offense against the other side's defense multiplicatively. Each team's offense and defense rate (points per possession) is shrunk toward a league prior with weight g / (g + 8), and a team's expected rate is its shrunk offense times the opponent's shrunk defense divided by the prior. The prior is 1.10 points per possession per team (2.20 combined; 8.8 is 8 times 1.10). That prior was set from a small early sample and may run high.

matchTotal is the original SIET formula, with denominator guards that do not change any value, so its earlier tracking record still applies. homeTotal = game pace * (Home shrunk offense * Away shrunk defense) / 1.1 + 1.6 and awayTotal = game pace * (Away shrunk offense * Home shrunk defense) / 1.1 - 1.6, so Home plus Away equals matchTotal before clamping. handicap is Home minus Away from those two pieces plus the 3.2-point home-court constant (borrowed from the app's validated example, not tuned). straightWin applies the algebraic sigmoid 0.5 + 0.48 * m / sqrt(190 + m squared) to that margin.

decision is value-oriented: 0.70 * opt.ev (capped at plus or minus 0.6) + 0.30 * (opt.prob - opt.implied_prob). It subtracts 0.8 per unit of opt.prob below 0.40, 0.3 per unit of odds below 1.40 and 0.15 per unit of odds above 3.50, so the #1, #2 and #3 picks reward estimated edge over price without chasing very unlikely outcomes. It has no market-type bonus.

Assumptions and limitations: season-to-date rates from 1 to 3 games are noisy and the shrinkage constants (weight 8, prior 1.10) are untuned guesses. Games against non-Division I opponents can inflate a team's rates. No SRS, SOS, injuries or roster changes are used, so missing ratings never cause NO DATA. The home-court constants are wrong for neutral-site games. Overtime is not modeled separately. No accuracy or profitability is claimed; it has only been tested on a small early-season log with no reliable edge shown.

PSIT works directly in points per game instead of possessions. Each team's points scored and points allowed are shrunk toward a league average of 75.75 points per team with a light weight of 2 / (g + 2), so a team's own scoring stays dominant. A team's expected score is its shrunk offense times the opponent's shrunk defense divided by 75.75, which lets a strong offense facing a weak defense be amplified. Pace and shooting are deliberately not used. The 75.75 level (151.5 combined) was set from an early-season sample and is not a general constant.

matchTotal is the original PSIT formula, unchanged, so its earlier tracking record still applies. homeTotal = Home shrunk offense * Away shrunk defense / 75.75 + 1.6 and awayTotal = Away shrunk offense * Home shrunk defense / 75.75 - 1.6, so Home plus Away equals matchTotal before clamping. handicap is Home minus Away from those two pieces plus the 3.2-point home-court constant (borrowed from the app's validated example, not tuned), limited to plus or minus 45. straightWin applies the algebraic sigmoid 0.5 + 0.48 * m / sqrt(190 + m squared) to that margin. Because the shrinkage is light, margins and win probabilities can be extreme early in the season, so treat the handicap and win slots as the least reliable.

decision is a balanced z-score ranker: 0.40 * opt.z / 2.5 (capped at plus or minus 1) + 0.60 * (opt.prob - 0.5) + 0.20 * opt.ev * 3 (capped at plus or minus 1). It adds 0.05 for the three totals markets, subtracts 0.04 for handicap and straight-win candidates because of the noisy margin, and subtracts 0.8 per unit of odds below 1.30 and 0.2 per unit of odds above 2.80.

Assumptions and limitations: season-to-date points from 1 to 3 games are noisy, and games against non-Division I opponents can inflate scoring and defense. There is no schedule-strength adjustment, no SRS, SOS, injuries or roster changes, so missing ratings never cause NO DATA. The home-court constants are wrong for neutral-site games. Overtime is not modeled separately. No accuracy or profitability is claimed; it has only been tested on a small early-season log with no reliable edge shown.

LRSV is a shot-volume model that pulls hot or cold shooting back toward average. Early in the season shooting percentages are mostly luck, while shot attempts, free-throw attempts and tempo are steadier. For each team it regresses field-goal efficiency (points per shot attempt) toward 1.007 and free-throw percentage toward 69.4%, multiplies by the real attempt counts to get regressed points, and divides by minutes played (home.mp, away.mp) to get a 40-minute rate, so overtime does not inflate it. The prior weights are untuned judgment calls: 400 combined field-goal attempts and 200 free-throw attempts in matchTotal.

matchTotal is the original LRSV formula, unchanged, so its earlier tracking record still applies. homeTotal = (Home regressed points per 40 minutes + Away regressed points allowed per 40 minutes) / 2 + 1.6 and awayTotal = (Away regressed points per 40 + Home regressed points allowed per 40) / 2 - 1.6. Here each team's own and opponent shooting are regressed separately at half the weights (200 field-goal attempts, 100 free-throw attempts), so Home plus Away only approximately matches matchTotal. handicap is Home minus Away from those pieces plus the 3.2-point home-court constant (borrowed from the app's validated example, not tuned). straightWin uses the linear form 0.5 + 0.035 * margin limited to 0.05 to 0.95, because the margin expression is too long to repeat inside a sigmoid.

decision is market-aware: 0.45 * (opt.prob - opt.implied_prob) + 0.35 * (opt.prob - 0.5) + 0.20 * opt.ev (capped at plus or minus 0.5). It adds 0.04 for match totals and 0.03 for home or away totals, subtracts 0.04 for straight win and 0.02 for handicap, and subtracts 1.2 per unit of odds below 1.30 and 0.3 per unit of odds above 2.60. That tilts the #1, #2 and #3 picks toward the totals markets this model is built around.

Assumptions and limitations: 1 to 3 games of shooting data are very noisy, the league averages come from a 365-team early-season table, and games against non-Division I opponents can inflate totals. It ignores SRS, SOS, schedule strength, injuries, roster changes and tempo matchups, so missing ratings never cause NO DATA. The home-court constants are wrong for neutral-site games. Its first clean pre-game test was weak, so no edge should be assumed. No accuracy or profitability is claimed.

Core thesis: Regresses team offensive and defensive efficiency toward league average using games played as the sample-size weight, then applies a blended pace factor and a calibrated home-court adjustment. Early-season numbers are pulled hard toward the mean; later-season numbers receive more weight. This reduces the extreme projections that pure possession models often produce in the first 8–12 games.

Scoreboard coherence: homeTotal and awayTotal are built from the same shrunk efficiency components so their sum closely tracks matchTotal and their difference tracks handicap. Straight-win probability is derived from the same margin used in the handicap formula via a smooth algebraic sigmoid.

Decision logic: Ranks candidates by a blend of raw edge (opt.prob - opt.implied_prob), absolute probability advantage, and a soft odds window that prefers prices between roughly 1.45 and 2.40. Extremely short or extremely long prices are down-weighted. model.trust is included so the ranking respects the app’s own Bayesian grading of the model on each market.

Assumptions and limitations: Relies only on season-long box-score aggregates available inside CourtQuant. No injury, rest, travel, or lineup data. Shrinkage prior is fixed (equivalent to ~10–12 games of league-average data). Performance must be judged by closing-line value and actual ROI, not by theoretical edge size. Early-season results remain higher variance even with shrinkage.

formulas.decision: ((opt.prob - opt.implied_prob) * 0.62 + (opt.prob - 0.5) * 0.28 + opt.ev * 0.10) * min(1.0, max(0.15, (opt.odds - 1.42) * 4.2)) * min(1.0, max(0.15, (2.55 - opt.odds) * 2.8)) * model.trust

models.description:
Designed and trained by Claude (Anthropic) on the 210-fixture capture audit (Nov 11-16, 2026) after backtesting all 15 existing models against real final scores. Core thesis: early-season totals are dominated by shooting luck, so shot volume (FGA, FTA, minutes) is trusted while conversion is regressed to league priors (the best-performing structure in the audit: Luck-Regressed Shot Volume), then recalibrated by -3.2 pts because every prior model and the books ran about 3.2-3.4 pts too high on totals. Margins are driven by schedule-aware ratings, not raw points: margin = 5.2 + 0.44 * SRS gap - 0.24 * SOS gap, where the negative SOS term strips schedule inflation that SRS carries early in the season. The 5.2 intercept is the measured home-court plus home-bias lift in this sample.

Interaction: matchTotal comes from the regressed shot-volume engine; handicap comes from the SRS/SOS margin; homeTotal and awayTotal are exactly (total + margin) / 2 and (total - margin) / 2, so Home + Away = Match Total and Home - Away = Handicap with no scoreboard contradictions. straightWin applies the algebraic sigmoid 0.5 + 0.48 * m / sqrt(250 + m^2) to the same margin (wider than the 190 constant because early margins are noisy). Backtest on captured results: total RMSE about 15.1 (raw best prior 15.5), margin RMSE 13.9 (best prior 15.8), team-score RMSE 10.9 home and 9.6 away, win log-loss 0.547 (best prior 0.582; bookmaker moneyline 0.51 is still sharper). A chronological split (fit on games up to Nov 13, test on later games) kept the same gains.

Decision AI: the audit showed prior models' probabilities were overconfident (model prob 0.86 hit only 52%) and that a model edge above 0.25 over the bookmaker lost money, so the ranker mostly trusts the bookmaker's implied probability and adds only 30% (scaled by model.trust, capped at +/-0.12) of the model's disagreement, plus a small Under tilt (+0.03; Over -0.03) measured from the sample. It blends 55% probability above 0.5 with 45% expected value, favors totals markets, mildly penalizes handicap and Straight Win, penalizes odds below 1.35 or above 2.2, and punishes edges above 0.25. pickGate passes a match when the adjusted probability clears about 0.66 and the edge is not extreme. In a paper-trade on the captured ladders, the #1 pick hit about 76% at roughly +8% ROI out of sample; treat this as an estimate, not a promise.

Assumptions and limitations: only 207 usable games with 2-5 games of stats each, so the offset, margin weights and Under tilt are early-season calibrations that should be re-fit as the season matures and books tighten. Handicap, Straight Win and both team totals need SRS and SOS and show NO DATA if either is missing (about 1.4% of games); Match O/U does not. Non-Division I opponents can distort stats, home-court is not adjusted for neutral sites, and overtime is only handled through minutes normalization. No profitability is guaranteed.

Designed by GitHub Copilot. This research-candidate model combines harmonic expected possessions with sample-size-shrunk offensive and opposing defensive points-per-possession estimates. The neutral prior is 1.02 points per possession, weighted with eight pseudo-games; the two teams' paces are combined harmonically to reduce the influence of extreme tempo mismatches.

Home and away score projections average each offense with the opponent's defense, then apply a modest +1.5/-1.5 home-court split. Match O/U uses the sum of those sibling score projections. The handicap blends that projected score margin (70%) with an SRS/SOS-adjusted margin (30%, including a +3.0 home-court term); Straight Win maps the sibling margin to a smooth bounded probability. Early-season missing SRS/SOS may leave rating-based formulas without data, as documented by CourtQuant.

Decision AI favors model probability over bookmaker implied probability and considers expected value, while smoothly down-weighting unusually short or long odds. Pick Gate admits only candidates whose probability exceeds both the implied probability and 52%, scaled by model.trust. This formula package is a candidate, not a proven winner: the repository SUMMARY reports 234 selection records across 216 fixtures and 214 checksum/match-valid receipts, but explicitly says receipt validity does not establish settlement or training eligibility. Therefore these captures do not support a defensible supervised backtest or a claim that this model outperforms the existing models. No historical recipes or capture records were changed.
